analysis.title: GS US TMT … quick hits … 17 Nov 2026
key_insights: NDX fell about 135 bps on 11/17 and re-tested its 11/5 intraday lows. The S&P 500 broke below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April, and defensive groups (pharma, healthcare, low-vol) also traded lower.

VIX moved through the 26 handle to the upside. ETFs were about 36% of the tape, well above recent trend, which the desk reads as top-down trading. GS PB data showed elevated short covering via macro products the prior week.

Semis are about 35% off their highs, with all 30 SOX components down in 2H CY26. The desk says debate on 2028+ growth rates looks like investors backing implied capex/GW growth rates out of stock prices, not a bottoms-up estimate revision.
All eyes are on NVDA earnings the evening of 11/17. The desk points to a GIR preview.
Top client inbounds: software weakness (CRM, HUBS, MDB), strength in SNAP and RDDT, positioning into NVDA, RBLX down 15% in 4 days (ahead of the GTA 6 launch), and TSM down 13% in 4 days.

DIS closed -1% after earnings, having been up about 2% for much of the day. Investor pushback is limited to SVOD questions and whether a reiteration of the FY27 outlook was enough after the stock's run. Bulls cite shareholder return updates (dividend, buyback, cost cuts) and domestic attendance +3% y/y on an adjusted basis in F4Q.
With DIS near $120, investors are asking how to compare it with NFLX using a chart of forward P/E for both.
Chart of the day points to the GIR 2027 outlook page, with the desk noting that the blue lines are moving in lock-step this cycle.

earnings_insights: DIS reported F4Q earnings on the morning of 11/17 and reiterated its FY27 outlook. The stock closed -1% after being up about 2% intraday. Domestic attendance was +3% y/y on an adjusted basis in F4Q. No EPS or revenue figures were given.
NVDA is scheduled to report the evening of 11/17. The desk gives no estimates.
risk_factors: NVDA earnings on the evening of 11/17 against a tape that has re-tested the 11/5 lows.
Semis down about 35% from highs with the growth-rate debate driven by price, not estimates.
Defensive sectors (pharma, healthcare, low-vol) are also falling, so there is limited shelter within equities.
